\section[o saldo]{o saldo — the balance (of an account)}

\label{lesson:PT-C393-saldo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the rate, then the Portuguese for the inflation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o saldo}
\textbf{o saldo} — \textquotedblleft{}the balance (of an account)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Vi o saldo da conta no multibanco.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I checked my account balance at the cash machine.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Os saldos} in the plural are the sales in shops.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{saldo} was borrowed from Italian \emph{saldo} \textquotedblleft{}balance, settled\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{saldare} \textquotedblleft{}to settle\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{solidus} \textquotedblleft{}solid, whole\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o saldo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o saldo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o saldo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the rate, then the Portuguese for the inflation, then say \emph{o saldo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o saldo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The balance (of an account)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o depósito]{o depósito — the deposit; the (fuel) tank}

\label{lesson:PT-C393-deposito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the inflation, then the Portuguese for the balance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o depósito}
\textbf{o depósito} — \textquotedblleft{}the deposit; the (fuel) tank\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fiz um depósito de cem euros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I made a deposit of a hundred euros.}
\end{quote}

Also a fuel tank: \emph{encher o depósito} — to fill up the tank.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{depósito} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dēpositum} \textquotedblleft{}a thing laid down for safekeeping\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{dēpōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to lay down\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{pōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to put\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the inflation, then the Portuguese for the balance, then say \emph{o depósito} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[depositar]{depositar — to deposit, to pay in}

\label{lesson:PT-C393-depositar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the balance, then the Portuguese for the deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: depositar}
\textbf{depositar} — \textquotedblleft{}to deposit, to pay in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Depositei o dinheiro na minha conta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I paid the money into my account.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Depositar um cheque} — to pay in a cheque.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{depositar} is built on \emph{depósito} \textquotedblleft{}deposit\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{dēpositum} \textquotedblleft{}a thing laid down for safekeeping\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), on \emph{pōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to put\textquotedblright{}.

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[transferir]{transferir — to transfer}

\label{lesson:PT-C393-transferir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the deposit, then the Portuguese for to deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: transferir}
\textbf{transferir} — \textquotedblleft{}to transfer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Transferi o dinheiro da renda para a conta da minha mãe.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I transferred the rent money to my mother's account.}
\end{quote}

Conjugated \emph{transfiro, transferes, transfere}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{transferir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{trānsferre} \textquotedblleft{}to carry across\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{trāns} \textquotedblleft{}across\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ferre} \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
